evidence.claim: The webinar presented Iran's child social-protection system, a welfare database for deprived households, and a cash-plus model for vulnerable children in selected provinces.
evidence.title: UNICEF and Ministry of Labour discussed enhancing social protection systems for children
evidence.excerpt: The webinar presented Iran's child social-protection system, a welfare database for deprived households, and a cash-plus model for vulnerable children in selected provinces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNICEF press release with specific program mechanics and named government counterparts.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to 2022 and explicitly about children's social protection.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful; the program ran through Iranian ministries under the regime, though this source does not isolate a Khamenei personal order.
contrary_evidence: The page describes plans and cooperation, not audited nationwide results.

evidence.claim: UNICEF provided 1,266 tablets for students with special needs nationwide to support online distance learning during pandemic school closures.
evidence.title: UNICEF Iran Provides 1,266 Tablets for Students with Special Needs
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF provided 1,266 tablets for students with special needs nationwide to support online distance learning during pandemic school closures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific 2022 press release with a concrete quantity, target group, and delivery mechanism.
evidence.period_fit: Close to the target period and tied to the COVID-school-closure legacy still affecting 2022 education access.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; delivered through UNICEF and the Ministry of Education, not a direct Khamenei order.
contrary_evidence: The action was compensatory and crisis-driven, so it shows mitigation more than structural reform.

evidence.claim: In 2022 UNICEF covered the screening costs for Afghan refugee children, nomad children, and children in disadvantaged provinces, helping 97,454 children and contributing to a dedicated public budget line and expansion to 750 centres.
evidence.title: UNICEF supports school entrance health screening for 1.5 million children in Iran
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 UNICEF covered the screening costs for Afghan refugee children, nomad children, and children in disadvantaged provinces, helping 97,454 children and contributing to a dedicated public budget line and expansion to 750 centres.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The page gives a precise 2022 implementation claim, named provinces, a child count, and institutional follow-on effects.
evidence.period_fit: The key implementation claim is explicitly about 2022, even though the page was published in 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but useful; it shows state service delivery under the regime, not personally Khamenei’s hand.
contrary_evidence: The page also shows the service had to be subsidized for disadvantaged groups, implying unequal baseline access.

evidence.claim: The survey reported 97.8 percent vaccination coverage for Iranian children and 90.3 percent for non-Iranian children, with 29 provinces at or above 95 percent.
evidence.title: Immunization coverage of children aged 24-35 months in the Islamic Republic of Iran: a national cluster coverage survey
evidence.publisher: WHO EMRO / East Mediterr Health J
evidence.excerpt: The survey reported 97.8 percent vaccination coverage for Iranian children and 90.3 percent for non-Iranian children, with 29 provinces at or above 95 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed WHO regional journal with exact quantitative findings and explicit national-program context.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and directly describes Iran's child-immunization system as a service-delivery baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly country-system context; it supports welfare assessment but does not by itself isolate Khamenei's personal contribution.
contrary_evidence: The non-Iranian coverage gap indicates uneven inclusion even within a strong national program.

evidence.claim: WHO said Iran's pandemic response was hampered by limited genomic sequencing capacity and low vaccination coverage, and that WHO and partners later mobilized vaccine doses and sequencing support.
evidence.title: Response to COVID-19 in Iran
evidence.excerpt: WHO said Iran's pandemic response was hampered by limited genomic sequencing capacity and low vaccination coverage, and that WHO and partners later mobilized vaccine doses and sequencing support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO country-story page gives a specific assessment of response constraints and remedial support, with explicit dates and quantities.
evidence.period_fit: Near-period evidence about a major health crisis still shaping 2022 welfare conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; it captures state capacity and crisis response under the regime rather than a direct Khamenei welfare order.
contrary_evidence: The page also documents external support and eventual scale-up, so it is not a pure failure story.

evidence.claim: The article says Iran exempts refugees from school fees, WFP provides school snacks and cash incentives for girls, and UNHCR has supported school construction, helping more than 500,000 Afghan children access education.
evidence.title: UNHCR and WFP help refugee children stay in school and reach for their dreams
evidence.excerpt: The article says Iran exempts refugees from school fees, WFP provides school snacks and cash incentives for girls, and UNHCR has supported school construction, helping more than 500,000 Afghan children access education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNHCR/WFP reporting with concrete service counts and policy details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to 2022 and tied to refugee welfare and education access.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful; it reflects state policy and UN-supported delivery under the Iranian regime, not a documented personal Khamenei instruction.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes that inflation still made school supplies unaffordable for many families, so access remained fragile.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said only a third of pandemic-period job losses had been recovered and that social-protection measures lacked targeting and inflation indexation, limiting their effect.
evidence.title: Iran's Economic Update — April 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said only a third of pandemic-period job losses had been recovered and that social-protection measures lacked targeting and inflation indexation, limiting their effect.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous World Bank country update with direct welfare-relevant findings and no need for inference on the economic side.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level welfare context, not a direct Khamenei policy finding, but relevant to life-chances under his rule.
contrary_evidence: The report acknowledges that social-protection measures did partially mitigate pressure, so it is mixed rather than purely negative.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on Khamenei's own 2022 command-and-control or safety governance is thin.
Risk-reduction evidence is mostly procedural rather than demonstrated durable restraint.
Proxy and drone-transfer evidence is strong on state conduct but weak on direct Khamenei ordering.
The diplomatic track is shown as a process, not a clearly completed peace or de-escalation achievement.
Direct personal orders are still sparse, so command-chain attribution remains system-level in places.
There was no 2022 election contestation event, so practice evidence for contestability is indirect.
Several strongest items are protest-repression evidence that overlaps heavily with Chapter 3B.
Direct Khamenei-attributed economic implementation evidence is thin relative to macro context.
Household and regional distribution effects are better described than attributed.
Direct ruler-attributed welfare decisions remain thin compared with UN/agency delivery material.
The package is stronger on refugees, children, and UN-supported programs than on the whole-population welfare picture.
Direct 2022 evidence on Khamenei's own assets, disclosures, gifts, or self-dealing remains absent.
Admissions of error, corrective behavior, and independent scrutiny are thin.
The plan-to-implementation chain is still incomplete.
Outcome evidence exists, but durable goal progress is only partly established and is confounded by sanctions, protests, and macro stress.
